aggressive_definition: Stage III or IV prostate cancer or Gleason score greater than 7
aggressive_definition_excerpt: We estimated the risk of prostate cancer using multivariate, conditional logistic regression to calculate odds ratios and 95% confidence intervals for overall prostate cancer and aggressive disease (stage III or IV or Gleason >7; n = 269).
study_design: Nested case-control study within the Prostate, Lung, Colorectal, and Ovarian Cancer Screening Trial
cohort_total_n_excerpt: We examined whether serum concentrations of retinol were associated with the risk of prostate cancer in a nested case-control study using 692 prostate cancer cases and 844 matched controls from the Prostate, Lung, Colorectal, and Ovarian Cancer Screening Trial.
reason: The abstract explicitly analyzes both overall prostate cancer and aggressive incident disease defined as stage III or IV or Gleason score greater than 7. It also reports a numeric estimate for the aggressive high-grade subset.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Serum retinol concentrations were not associated with overall prostate cancer risk; however, the highest versus lowest concentrations of serum retinol were associated with a 42% reduction in aggressive prostate cancer risk (P(trend) = 0.02), with the strongest inverse association for high-grade disease (Gleason sum >7; odds ratio, 0.52; 95% confidence interval, 0.32-0.84; P(trend) = 0.01).
estimate_classifications.reason: The supplied OR of 0.80 is explicitly identified by existing evidence as the overall prostate cancer estimate. It must not be relabeled aggressive merely because the article also analyzes aggressive disease.

additional_estimates.comparison: Highest versus lowest concentrations of serum retinol
additional_estimates.effect_excerpt: Serum retinol concentrations were not associated with overall prostate cancer risk; however, the highest versus lowest concentrations of serum retinol were associated with a 42% reduction in aggressive prostate cancer risk (P(trend) = 0.02), with the strongest inverse association for high-grade disease (Gleason sum >7; odds ratio, 0.52; 95% confidence interval, 0.32-0.84; P(trend) = 0.01).
